summary: The paper addresses similarity measurement between incomplete data samples, where traditional deletion or imputation-based approaches lose information or introduce bias. It proposes the proximity kernel, which combines equal-frequency binning, proximity (Voronoi) assignment, one-hot encoding, and a three-level cascading fallback strategy using kernel mean embedding for missing features. Experiments on 12 UCI incomplete datasets show the proposed method achieves the highest average NMI of 0.4245, best or second-best NMI on 10 of 12 datasets, and linear time complexity in the number of samples.

approach: Reimplement the proximity kernel from the paper for the target claim C1 on the UCI Hepatitis dataset. For each feature, equal-frequency binning uses evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values only, then each observed value is assigned to its nearest bin center and encoded as a one-hot vector. Missing feature encodings are filled by a three-level cascading fallback (intersection matching, union matching, global prior) using kernel mean embedding over matching samples. The resulting representation Z is clustered with sklearn KMeans using the ground-truth number of clusters, NMI is averaged over 10 random seeds, and nbins is searched over {2,3,4,6,8} by mean NMI. Finally, reproduce.py writes results/metrics.json comparing the selected NMI to the target 0.2289 within ±0.02.
steps: Setup: confirm numpy, pandas, scikit-learn are installed. No extra packages are required because pandas can read the UCI URL directly. Set all random seeds via the seed lists in config.

Implement src/data.py: read https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data with pandas.read_csv(header=None, na_values=['?', '']); X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).values; y = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(int).values - 1; assert X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), len(np.unique(y)) == 2; return X, y, K=2.

Implement src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins(X, nbins): for each feature j, obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]; if len(obs) == 0, centers = None and prior = uniform 1/nbins; else centers = np.percentile(obs, 100*np.arange(1, nbins+1)/(nbins+1), method='linear'); store centers and global prior frequencies.

Implement proximity_kernel.py assign_bins(X, centers): for each observed value, k = np.argmin(np.abs(x - centers)); tie breaks to lowest index; store integer bin assignments B (n, d) with -1 for missing entries.
Implement proximity_kernel.py encode_observed(B, nbins): build H_obs (n, d, nbins) with H_obs[i, j, B[i, j]] = 1 for observed entries, zeros for missing entries.

Implement proximity_kernel.py compute_fallback_encodings(X, B, H_obs, centers, nbins): for each missing entry (i, j), let O_i = observed features of i and B_i = B[i, O_i]. Level 1: S1 = {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l] for all l in O_i}; S1_j = {m in S1 : X[m, j] observed}; if S1_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S1_j). Level 2: if S1_j empty, S2 = union_{l in O_i} {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l]}; S2_j = {m in S2 : X[m, j] observed}; if S2_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S2_j). Level 3: if S2_j empty, h = global prior for feature j (bin frequencies among observed values, or uniform 1/nbins if feature entirely missing). Store H[i, j] = h and record level counts.

Implement proximity_kernel.py build_representation(X, nbins): call fit_bins, assign_bins, encode_observed, compute_fallback_encodings; concatenate H[i, j] across j to get Z (n, d*nbins); return Z and diagnostics including missing entry count and level 1/2/3 counts.
Implement proximity_kernel.py proximity_kernel(Z): return K = Z @ Z.T / d where d = 19; use only for symmetry and bounds checks.

Implement src/cluster.py evaluate_nbins(Z, y, K, seeds): for each seed, run KMeans(n_clusters=K, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=seed).fit(Z); labels = kmeans.labels_; nmi = normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels); return mean, std, per-seed list.

Implement src/cluster.py search_nbins(X, y, K, nbins_grid, seeds): for each nbins in nbins_grid, call build_representation, evaluate_nbins, and record mean/std/per-seed; select best nbins as the one with highest mean NMI; return best_nbins, best_mean, all_results.

Implement reproduce.py: parse optional --smoke flag. If smoke, load data, subset first 20 rows, run build_representation with nbins=2, assert Z.shape == (20, 38), assert no NaN/inf, assert each observed-feature one-hot sums to 1 and each missing-feature fallback vector sums to 1, compute K and assert symmetry and diagonal <= 1, run one KMeans with seed 0, print NMI and diagnostics. Otherwise run search_nbins on full Hepatitis with nbins_grid and seeds.
Run smoke test: python reproduce.py --smoke. Verify output shows correct shapes, no NaNs, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, and a valid NMI in [0, 1].

Run intermediate checks before full run: print X shape (155, 19), y shape (155,), class counts, total missing entries and per-feature missing counts; verify bin centers are strictly increasing for features with observed values; verify B indices are in [0, nbins-1]; verify H row sums per feature are 1 for all samples; print fallback level counts (level 3 should be rare, <5% of missing entries); verify K is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, K_ij in [0, 1]; run a sanity baseline KMeans on median-imputed raw features and record its NMI for reference.
Run full reproduction: python reproduce.py. This runs 5 nbins values × 10 seeds = 50 KMeans runs on 155 samples; each run is seconds or less.

Inspect results/metrics.json: check the C1 value, best_nbins, per-nbins means, and per-seed NMI spread. Compare |value - 0.2289| <= 0.02. If outside tolerance, run sensitivity variants: (a) percentile centers at 100*(k-0.5)/nbins; (b) percentile centers at 100*k/nbins; (c) kernel K-means assigning each point to the cluster maximizing average K to cluster members. Record each variant's value and choose the most faithful documented variant; otherwise keep the primary result.
Finalize results/metrics.json with the chosen C1 value, target 0.2289, tolerance 0.02, pass/fail boolean, best nbins, per-nbins and per-seed results, diagnostics, runtime, and environment metadata.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke: loads Hepatitis, subsets first 20 rows, builds Z with nbins=2, checks Z shape == (20, 38), no NaN/inf, each feature encoding sums to 1 per sample, kernel K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric with diagonal <= 1, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, runs KMeans(n_clusters=2, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=0), and prints an NMI in [0, 1].
intermediate_checks: Dataset size: X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), number of classes == 2.
Class balance: print counts of y == 0 and y == 1 (expected approximately 32/123 for Hepatitis; exact counts are fine).
Missingness: total number of NaN entries and per-feature NaN counts; confirm common UCI missing markers '?' were converted to NaN.
Binning: for each feature with observed values, the nbins bin centers are strictly increasing; for any entirely missing feature, uniform prior is used.
Proximity assignment: all non-missing bin indices B[i, j] are in [0, nbins-1]; missing entries are -1.
One-hot encoding: for every sample and every feature, the encoding vector h_{i,j} sums to 1 (exactly 1 for observed, probabilities summing to 1 for missing).
Fallback diagnostics: count missing entries resolved by level 1, level 2, and level 3; level 3 should be rare (<5% of missing entries).
Kernel matrix: K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, and all entries are in [0, 1].
Sanity baseline: KMeans on raw features with median imputation gives some NMI; record it to ensure the proximity kernel result is not identical to a trivial imputation baseline.
Parameter count: Z has shape (155, 19*nbins); for nbins in {2,3,4,6,8} this is 38, 57, 76, 114, 152 features.
budget_plan: Total ~15-20 min for target C1: setup and dependency check 2 min, data download and parsing 1 min, implementation of data/proximity_kernel/cluster 5 min, smoke test 1 min, intermediate checks and diagnostics 3 min, full 5 nbins × 10 seeds KMeans/NMI run on 155 samples 5 min, write and verify results/metrics.json 2 min. C2-C8 are out of scope for this plan because they require 12 datasets and would take hours; the code is dataset-agnostic if extended.

"""Data loading for the UCI incomplete datasets used in the paper (Table 2).

Only the target dataset (Hepatitis, claim C1) is downloaded by default.
Raw files are cached under $REPRO_DATA_CACHE so repeated runs do not re-download.

import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

    "REPRO_DATA_CACHE", os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".cache", "datasets", "files")
)

# UCI "machine-learning-databases" flat files (no unzip needed).
UCI_URLS = {
    "hepatitis": "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data",
}

# Column 0 of hepatitis.data is the class label (1 = DIE, 2 = LIVE).
HEPATITIS_LABEL_COL = 0


def _cache_path(name: str) -> str:
    return os.path.join(CACHE_DIR, "uci", name, os.path.basename(UCI_URLS[name]))


def _download(name: str) -> str:
    """Download a raw UCI file into the shared cache (idempotent)."""
    import urllib.request

"""K-means clustering + NMI evaluation of the proximity-kernel representation.

Paper Section 5.1 (Evaluation Protocol):
  * K-means with the number of clusters set to the ground-truth number of classes
  * NMI as the clustering metric
  * each experiment run 10 times, average reported
  * nbins searched over {2, 3, 4, 6, 8}

from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.metrics import normalized_mutual_info_score

from src.proximity_kernel import NBINS_GRID, build_representation

SEEDS = list(range(10))


def evaluate_representation(Z, y, n_clusters, seeds=SEEDS, n_init=10):
    """Run K-means on the representation Z for each seed; return per-seed NMIs."""
    per_seed = []
    for seed in seeds:
        km = KMeans(n_clusters=n_clusters, init="k-means++", n_init=n_init, random_state=seed)
        labels = km.fit_predict(Z)
        per_seed.append(float(normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels)))
    per_seed = np.asarray(per_seed, dtype=float)
    return {
        "nmi_mean": float(per_seed.mean()),
        "nmi_std": float(per_seed.std(ddof=0)),
        "nmi_best": float(per_seed.max()),
        "nmi_worst": float(per_seed.min()),
        "per_seed": [float(v) for v in per_seed],
    }


def search_nbins(X, y, n_clusters, nbins_grid=NBINS_GRID, seeds=SEEDS, n_init=10,
                 fallback_variant="observed_only"):
    """Search nbins over the grid; select the value with the highest mean NMI."""
    results = {}
    for nbins in nbins_grid:
        Z, diag = build_representation(X, nbins, fallback_variant=fallback_variant)
        res = evaluate_representation(Z, y, n_clusters, seeds=seeds, n_init=n_init)
        res["diagnostics"] = diag
        results[int(nbins)] = res
    best_nbins = max(results, key=lambda k: results[k]["nmi_mean"])
    return best_nbins, results

"""Sensitivity checks (not part of reproduce.py): verify the primary configuration is
robust and document how the C1 value moves under alternative readings of the paper."""
import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.metrics import normalized_mutual_info_score

from src.data import load_hepatitis
from src.proximity_kernel import build_representation, bin_centers, assign_bins

X, y = load_hepatitis()
n, d = X.shape
K = 2
seeds = list(range(10))


def nmi(Z):
    vals = []
    for s in seeds:
        km = KMeans(n_clusters=K, init="k-means++", n_init=10, random_state=s)
        vals.append(normalized_mutual_info_score(y, km.fit_predict(Z)))
    return float(np.mean(vals)), float(np.std(vals)), float(np.max(vals))


print("=== fallback variants (paper Eq.4 centers) ===")
for variant in ["observed_only", "prior_filled", "iterative"]:
    for nbins in [2, 3, 4, 6, 8]:
        Z, diag = build_representation(X, nbins, fallback_variant=variant)
        m, s, b = nmi(Z)
        print(f"  {variant:14s} nbins={nbins}  mean={m:.4f} std={s:.4f} best={b:.4f} "
              f"L1/L2/L3={diag['level1_entries']}/{diag['level2_entries']}/{diag['level3_entries']}")

print("\n=== alternative bin-center formulas (observed_only fallback) ===")


def build_alt(X, nbins, mode):
    obs = ~np.isnan(X)
    H = np.zeros((n, d, nbins))
    priors = []
    for j in range(d):
        vals = X[obs[:, j], j]
        if vals.size == 0:
            priors.append(np.full(nbins, 1.0 / nbins))
            H[:, j, :] = priors[j]
            continue
        if mode == "paper":          # (k-1)*100/(nbins-1)
            pct = 100.0 * np.arange(nbins) / (nbins - 1)
        elif mode == "midpoint":     # (k-0.5)*100/nbins
            pct = 100.0 * (np.arange(nbins) + 0.5) / nbins
        elif mode == "k/(nbins+1)":  # plan assumption A13
            pct = 100.0 * np.arange(1, nbins + 1) / (nbins + 1)
        c = np.percentile(vals, pct, method="linear")
        b = assign_bins(vals, c)
        H[obs[:, j], j, b[obs[:, j]]] = 1.0
        cnt = np.bincount(b, minlength=nbins).astype(float)
        priors.append(cnt / cnt.sum())
    # fallback (observed_only)
    B = np.full((n, d), -1, dtype=int)
    for j in range(d):
        idx = np.where(obs[:, j])[0]
        if idx.size:
            vals = X[idx, j]
            c = bin_centers(vals, nbins)
            B[idx, j] = assign_bins(vals, c)
    for i in range(n):
        miss = np.where(~obs[i])[0]
        if miss.size == 0:
            continue
        ob = np.where(obs[i])[0]
        s1 = None
        s2 = set()
        for j in ob:
            mem = set(np.where(B[:, j] == B[i, j])[0].tolist())
            mem.discard(i)
            s1 = mem if s1 is None else (s1 & mem)
            s2 |= mem
        s1 = np.array(sorted(s1), dtype=int)
        s2 = np.array(sorted(s2), dtype=int)
        for j in miss:
            sel = s1[obs[s1, j]] if s1.size else np.array([], dtype=int)
            if sel.size:
                H[i, j, :] = H[sel, j, :].mean(axis=0)
                continue
            sel = s2[obs[s2, j]] if s2.size else np.array([], dtype=int)
            if sel.size:
                H[i, j, :] = H[sel, j, :].mean(axis=0)
                continue
            H[i, j, :] = priors[j]
    return H.reshape(n, d * nbins)


for mode in ["paper", "midpoint", "k/(nbins+1)"]:
    for nbins in [2, 3, 4, 6, 8]:
        Z = build_alt(X, nbins, mode)
        m, s, b = nmi(Z)
        print(f"  centers={mode:14s} nbins={nbins}  mean={m:.4f} std={s:.4f} best={b:.4f}")

print("\n=== cluster structure at nbins=2 (primary) ===")
Z, _ = build_representation(X, 2)
km = KMeans(n_clusters=K, init="k-means++", n_init=10, random_state=0).fit(Z)
lab = km.labels_
print("  cluster sizes:", np.bincount(lab))
print("  class sizes  :", np.bincount(y))
print("  NMI          : %.4f" % normalized_mutual_info_score(y, lab))
print("  purity       : %.4f" % max(
    (np.bincount(y[lab == c], minlength=2).max() / (lab == c).sum()) for c in range(K)))

Reproduced claim C1 exactly: the proximity kernel ("Ours") achieves NMI 0.2289 on the UCI Hepatitis dataset under K-means with the ground-truth number of clusters (K=2), matching the paper's Table 3 value to 4 decimal places (abs error 0.0, tolerance 0.02).

What was built (from the paper only; no author code was available):
- src/data.py — loads UCI Hepatitis (155x19, 2 classes 32/123, 167 missing entries = 5.67% over the 19 features, matching Table 2) from the cached raw file in $REPRO_DATA_CACHE, converting '?'/blank to NaN.
- src/proximity_kernel.py — equal-frequency bin centers as evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values only (paper Eq. 4, so c_{j,1}/c_{j,nbins} are the min/max), proximity assignment to the nearest center with ties to the lowest index (Eq. 5), one-hot encoding concatenated over features (Eqs. 6-7), and the three-level cascading fallback: level-1 intersection matching + kernel mean embedding (Eqs. 8-10), level-2 union matching + KME (Eqs. 11-12), level-3 global bin prior (Eqs. 13-14). Kernel K = (1/d) Z Z^T (Eq. 15).
- src/cluster.py — sklearn KMeans (k-means++, n_init=10) on the representation Z with n_clusters = ground-truth K, NMI averaged over 10 seeds, nbins searched over {2,3,4,6,8} and selected by highest mean NMI.
- reproduce.py — entrypoint with a --smoke structural test (shapes, finite values, per-feature encodings summing to 1, kernel symmetry/bounds/PSD, valid NMI) and the full run that writes results/metrics.json.

Result: nbins=2 selected; mean NMI over 10 runs = 0.2289 (std 0.0, best-of-10 also 0.2289). Fallback diagnostics: 61 level-1, 106 level-2, 0 level-3 entries. Kernel is symmetric, entries in [0.203, 1.0], min eigenvalue ~ -2.6e-14 (PSD). Clustering is non-degenerate (cluster sizes 65/90, purity 0.9667); a median-imputation K-means sanity baseline gives NMI 0.0024, so the result is not a trivial imputation artifact. Runtime 2.8 s end-to-end (well under the 20-minute clean re-run limit); the run is deterministic and re-runnable from a clean results/ folder.

Sensitivity checks (run separately, not part of reproduce.py) confirmed the primary configuration is the faithful one: all three KME-fallback readings (observed-only, prior-filled, iterative) give 0.2289 at nbins=2, while the alternative bin-center formulas (midpoint percentiles, or 100*k/(nbins+1) as the draft plan's A13 suggested) give 0.1762 and 0.1907 — i.e. the paper's explicit Eq. (4) endpoint percentiles are required for the match. Per the manager's instruction I stopped here and did not build C2-C8 or add datasets.

Assumptions recorded (paper does not pin these down): categorical features ordinal-encoded and treated as numeric with no scaling (A1); linear percentile interpolation (A2); argmin ties to the lowest bin index (A3); sklearn KMeans k-means++/n_init=10 with seeds 0-9 (A4); sklearn arithmetic-mean NMI (A5); '?'/blank treated as missing (A6); uniform prior for an entirely-missing feature (A7); KME restricted to matching samples with feature j observed (A8); nbins selected per dataset by 10-run mean NMI (A9); transductive full-dataset clustering (A10). One deviation from the draft plan: the plan's A13 bin-center formula (100*k/(nbins+1)) contradicts the paper's Eq. (4), so the paper's formula was used — this is what reproduces the target exactly. The plan note claiming the paper reports best-of-10 rather than the mean was not followed: the paper text says "conducted 10 times and report average results", so the mean is the primary value and the best-of-10 is also reported in metrics.json (both are 0.2289 here).
